   137	    // A deadline suffix skips an arbitrary expired backlog in one seek.
   138	    pub(super) fn refuse_live_children(
   139	        &mut self,
   140	        parent: &str,
   141	        id: &Value,
   142	    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   143	        let children: Vec<_> = self
   144	            .schema
   145	            .children(parent)
   146	            .map(|(n, _, _)| n.clone())
   147	            .collect();
   148	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }
   149	        let now = self
   150	            .context
   151	            .now
   152	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   153	        let heap = children
   154	            .iter()
   155	            .map(|n| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[n]).saturating_mul(3))
   156	            .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   157	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — three schema-fixed seeks per child table, each drawn from the request's physical allowance.
   158	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::Steps, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {

   160	                let occupied = runner.device_work(|runner| runner.current_children(parent, id, &children))?;
   161	                return if occupied { Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent)) } else { Ok(()) };
   162	            }
   163	            for name in &children {
   164	                let never = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone(), Value::Null], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?;

    84	            return table.indexes.contains_key(through::CHILDREN).then_some(through::CHILDREN);
    85	        }
    86	        // The effective deadline: a read-through child's `$deadline`, else `expire at`.
    87	        let deadline = table.expiry_column();

    95	    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    96	    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    97	    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    98	    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    99	    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   100	        let table = self.table(child)?;
   101	        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
   102	            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),

   104	        });

   110	    /// `set null` reference's own cap does (a null reference has no parent).
   111	    pub fn cap_skips_null(&self, table: &Table, by: &[String], group: &[Value]) -> bool {

   115	    /// The tables a delete of a `parent` row may write through its writing
   116	    /// actions, and the tables its actions read. A function of the schema, so
   117	    /// a commit's touched set never says which of them a delete reached.
   118	    pub fn action_tables(&self, parent: &str) -> ActionTables {
   119	        let mut out = ActionTables::default();
   120	        let mut queue = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   121	        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
   122	        while let Some(table) = queue.pop() {
   123	            if !visited.insert(table.clone()) { continue; }
   124	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
   125	                out.read.insert(r.child.to_owned());
   126	                if r.action.writes() { out.written.insert(r.child.to_owned()); }
   127	                if r.action == OnDelete::Cascade { queue.push(r.child.to_owned()); }
   128	            }
   129	        }
   130	        // What a write of each of those tables writes in turn: the derived
   131	        // destinations `row_changed` names (aggregate targets, maintained-column
   132	        // owners, row-keyed views).
   133	        let derived: Vec<String> = self.maintains.iter().filter(|m| out.written.contains(&m.source) || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| out.written.contains(&k.table)))
   134	            .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.clone()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.clone())]).flatten().collect();
   135	        out.written.extend(derived);
   136	        out.written.retain(|name| self.visible(name));
   137	        // Private derivations disappear from the device's projection; their
   138	        // event envelope is exported with each direct source's write price.
   139	        let sources: Vec<String> = out.written.iter().cloned().collect();
   140	        for source in sources {
   141	            if let Some(events) = self.write_reservation(&source).and_then(|plan| plan.action_events) { out.written.extend(events.tables); }
   142	        }
   143	        out
   144	    }

   146	    /// The order a delete's closure is removed in: a row before any table it
   147	    /// must not outlive — its cascade parent, and its `read through` parent.
   148	    /// A cycle through those edges has no valid order and is refused.
   149	    pub fn deletion_precedes(&self, child: &str, parent: &str) -> bool {
   150	        self.table(child).is_some_and(|t| t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|through| through.parent == parent))
   151	            || self.referencing(parent).into_iter().any(|r| r.child == child && r.action == OnDelete::Cascade)
   152	    }
   153	
   154	    /// A table that reaches itself through cascade and `read through` edges.
   155	    pub fn deletion_cycle(&self) -> Option<String> {
   156	        fn visit<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, name: &'a str, path: &mut Vec<&'a str>, done: &mut BTreeSet<&'a str>) -> Option<String> {
   157	            if path.contains(&name) { return Some(name.to_owned()); }
   158	            if !done.insert(name) { return None; }
   159	            path.push(name);
   160	            for (child, _) in &schema.tables {
   161	                if schema.deletion_precedes(child, name) && let Some(cycle) = visit(schema, child, path, done) { return Some(cycle); }
   162	            }
   163	            path.pop();
   164	            None
   165	        }
   166	        let mut done = BTreeSet::new();
   167	        self.tables.keys().find_map(|name| if self.tables[name].on_delete.values().any(|a| *a == OnDelete::Cascade) || self.is_referenced(name) {
   168	            let mut path = Vec::new();
   169	            visit(self, name, &mut path, &mut done)
   170	        } else { None })
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    /// Whether `name` is a table a timeline orders the writes of.
   174	    pub fn timeline_member(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
   175	        self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name) || t.maps(name) || t.authors.first().is_some_and(|a| a == name))
   176	    }
   177	
   178	    /// The most rows of each table one delete of a `parent` row can reach
   179	    /// through its cascades (its closure), the root included: each cascade
   180	    /// edge multiplies by its cap, and edges into a table add up. `None` when
   181	    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
   182	    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {
   183	        // Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.
   184	        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   185	        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
   186	        let mut at = 0;
   187	        while at < reach.len() {
   188	            let table = reach[at].clone();
   189	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
   190	                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
   191	                let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   192	                let child = reach.iter().position(|t| t == r.child).unwrap_or_else(|| { reach.push(r.child.to_owned()); reach.len() - 1 });
   193	                edges.push((at, child, cap));
   194	            }
   195	            at += 1;
   196	        }
   197	        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
   198	        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
   199	        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
   200	        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
   201	        bounds[0] = 1;
   202	        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();
   203	        let mut done = 0;
   204	        while let Some(table) = ready.pop() {
   205	            done += 1;
   206	            for &(from, child, cap) in edges.iter().filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == table) {
   207	                bounds[child] = bounds[child].saturating_add(bounds[from].saturating_mul(cap));
   208	                indegree[child] -= 1;
   209	                if indegree[child] == 0 { ready.push(child); }
   210	            }
   211	        }
   212	        (done == reach.len()).then(|| reach.into_iter().zip(bounds).collect())
   213	    }

   215	    /// The fixed charge a delete of a `parent` row reserves before it probes,
   216	    /// cascades or clears any row, over every meter: the closure's rows and
   217	    /// their identities, every restrict probe (one seek per closure row, plus
   218	    /// the closure rows it skips), every set-null row, and one engine write of
   219	    /// each, priced from the source-write plan the engine already exports. A
   220	    /// function of the schema only — caps, the reference graph, each table's
   221	    /// indexes and row size, and the exported plans — so a meter, an `E_BOUND`
   222	    /// abort or the physical allowance never depends on how many (hidden) rows
   223	    /// exist, and every host charges alike: a device's projection keeps every
   224	    /// table that can carry an action and every exported price. `None` when the
   225	    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no
   226	    /// fixed write price. Heap is the closure's identity scratch plus the largest
   227	    /// single row's transient work, plus event images retained until commit.
   228	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — the reservation is schema-fixed; LLP 3000.015 §2's law for work shaped by hidden rows.
   229	    pub fn delete_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   230	        let bounds = self.closure_bounds(parent)?;
   231	        let mut price = [0_u64; 7];
   232	        let mut heap = 0_u64;
   233	        let mut identities = 0_u64;
   234	        let mut gathered = 0_u64;
   235	        let rows_of = |name: &str| bounds.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == name).map_or(0, |(_, n)| *n);
   236	        for (table, n) in &bounds {
   237	            let n = *n;
   238	            if table != parent {
   239	                // Fetched by the closure walk and again, current, before its delete.
   240	                let unit = self.unit_write(table)?;
   241	                heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   242	                add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n)));
   243	                identities = identities.saturating_add(n);
   244	                // Before any set-null write, each reached cascade row proves
   245	                // that no physically retained read-through child lies outside
   246	                // the closure. Each child table can skip every reached
   247	                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside
   248	                // witness. Execution performs
   249	                // these probes under reference_prepaid, so their complete
   250	                // schema bound belongs in this outer admission reservation.
   251	                let through_children: Vec<_> = self.children(table).collect();
   252	                let probes_per_row = through_children.iter()
   253	                    .map(|(child, _, _)| rows_of(child).saturating_add(1))
   254	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   255	                let probes = n.saturating_mul(probes_per_row);
   256	                add(&mut price, [probes, 0, probes, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   257	                let outside_heap = through_children.iter()
   258	                    .map(|(name, child, _)| crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(rows_of(name).saturating_add(1)))
   259	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   260	                heap = heap.max(outside_heap);
   261	            }
   262	            for r in self.referencing(table) {
   263	                // A capped walk holds one page of child images per seek.
   264	                let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(r.table);
   265	                heap = heap.max(row.saturating_mul(REFERENCE_PAGE as u64));
   266	                let seeks = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && r.table.through.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t.reference != r.column) { 2 } else { 1 };
   267	                // A walk over a capped group: a seek per page, and a last, short page per range.
   268	                let walk = |cap: u64| seeks * n + cap.saturating_mul(n) / REFERENCE_PAGE as u64;
   269	                // Every reached row runs the lifetime hook for every through
   270	                // child, including children the closure already cascaded away.
   271	                let through = r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column);
   272	                if through && table != parent { add(&mut price, [3_u64, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n))); }
   273	                match r.action {
   274	                    // A read-through child's probe: three seeks per closure row (LLP 3000.014 §6).
   275	                    OnDelete::Restrict if through => {},
   276	                    // One probe per closure row, a row per seek: it may skip the closure
   277	                    // rows that name it (each names one target per reference), then stops
   278	                    // at its first outside witness.
   279	                    OnDelete::Restrict => {
   280	                        let probe = seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n;
   281	                        add(&mut price, [2 * probe, probe, seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   282	                    }
   283	                    OnDelete::Cascade => {
   284	                        let pages = walk(u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?));
   285	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   286	                    }
   287	                    OnDelete::SetNull => {
   288	                        let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   289	                        gathered = gathered.max(cap);
   290	                        let cleared = cap.saturating_mul(n);
   291	                        let unit = self.unit_write(r.child)?;
   292	                        heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   293	                        let pages = walk(cap);
   294	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   295	                        add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(cleared)));
   296	                    }
   297	                    OnDelete::Keep => {}
   298	                }
   299	            }
   300	        }
   301	        // The root is read again, current, before its own removal.
   302	        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
   303	        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
   304	        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
   305	        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.
   306	        price[4] = heap.saturating_add(identities.saturating_add(1 + REFERENCE_PAGE as u64 + gathered).saturating_mul(CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES));

   308	        for (table, _) in &bounds {
   309	            for reference in self.referencing(table) {
   310	                if reference.action.writes() { receiver_steps = receiver_steps.max(self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?.steps_per_write); }
   311	            }
   312	        }
   313	        price[0] = price[0].saturating_add(price[3].saturating_mul(receiver_steps));
   314	        price[4] = price[4].saturating_add(self.retained_action_heap(parent, price[3])?);
   315	        Some(price)
   316	    }

   318	    /// Diagnostic recipe price: action work plus the root's ordinary write.
   319	    /// Execution retains its existing separate charges for these two terms.
   320	    pub fn delete_total_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   321	        let mut total = self.delete_reservation(parent)?;
   322	        add(&mut total, self.unit_write(parent)?);
   323	        Some(total)
   324	    }
   325	
   326	    /// Event images remain live until commit, after action scratch is released.
   327	    pub fn delete_event_heap(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<u64> {

- **The decision of 2026-09-13** (LLP 3000 §7) says a reference validates the
  id's value; insert, update and upsert do not read the target; and
  "deleting it neither cascades nor refuses because references remain". This
  RFC replaces the last clause and keeps the rest: **a reference is still not
  an existence check at write time.** A row may be inserted naming an id that
  does not exist, is hidden, or lives in another partition, exactly as today;
  `require exists t[ref] else CODE` remains the explicit form (§4.4 says what
  this leaves open). What changes is what happens to the rows that reference
  a row **at the moment it is deleted**.

The integrity claim is therefore precise and modest: **when a delete of row
`p` executes, every live row that references `p` at that moment through a
`restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference is refused for, deleted, or
cleared.** It is not "no dangling reference ever exists": a later statement,
even in the same mutation, may insert a row naming `p`, and a `keep`
reference, an excluded reference kind (§2.1) or an expired parent still
leaves the referencing row in place.

## 2. The form

```
column: <table> [?] [on delete restrict | on delete cascade | on delete set null | on delete keep] [default …] [written by …]
```

`on delete` follows the type (and its `?`). One spelling; no `on update`
(ids are immutable).

### 2.1 Which references carry an action

A reference **carries an action** when both ends are ordinary durable
tables: the child (the table declaring the column) and the parent (the
table it names) are neither ephemeral nor engine-owned (maintained views,
private maintained state, timeline-owned tables, and a receipt family's
scope, members and runs tables). Every reference that carries an action has
one: the declared one, or `restrict`.

A reference that does not carry an action keeps today's meaning (the row
stays) and declaring `on delete` on it is `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`:

| Child or parent | Why no action |
|---|---|
| ephemeral child or parent | ephemeral rows live for seconds and are retired by the engine on its own clock; probing or cascading them would make durable deletes depend on presence |
| engine-owned child or parent | the engine derives or orders these rows; no program writes or deletes them on its own (a receipt scope is deletable only by the system) |
| a field-owned column (`written by`) | its value belongs to its writers' audience, not to the table's rules; probing, clearing or cascading through it would disclose or write a field only its owner may (LLP 3000.007's field authority), so the binder gives it no reference index |

The integrity of §1 and the migration of §8 therefore cover every reference
**that carries an action**. A field-owned reference keeps today's meaning,
as a reference into an ephemeral table does: it may name a deleted row, and a
read must treat its target as possibly absent.

### 2.2 Eligibility of each action

| Action | Requires | Refused |
|---|---|---|
| `restrict` | nothing | — |
| `keep` | nothing | — (no index, no probe, no read gate) |
| `cascade` | `cap N by <column>` on the child (exactly that column), or a plain single-column `unique <column>` key (an inferred effective bound of one) | without either bound: `E_CASCADE_BOUND`. A composite unique key does not bound one reference group. With `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`: a cycle in the cascade graph, including a self-reference, or in the union of cascade and `read through` edges (§3 step 6); a child that is `append only`, has any field-owned (`written by`) column, has a derived synced destination that delivers private fields to their owners, feeds a maintained `sum` (view or column), plays any role in a timeline (owned, mapped or authors), is a row-keyed view's member table (its writes may recount a group outside any fixed price), or whose source writes have no fixed price (a `server_only` reservation plan, LLP 3000.022 §14.3); a `read through` reference whose child can carry a finite effective deadline (§6.1). |
| `set null` | an optional (`?`) reference; either `cap N by <column>` or the same single-column unique inference, whose effective bound is one | everything refused for `cascade` except the cycle rule (set null does not recurse), and a column that **carries authority or meaning anywhere in the schema**: `immutable`, `written by`, a `sequence` parent, the root of a recorded or maintained path (`.column.field`), read by **any** rule of **any** table — the child's own read and write rules (directly or as the first hop of `.column.field`), every other table's `exists`/`created` probe that keys or equates on it, and every rule's hop that passes through it (`.task.column`) — named by the child's `sync` audience or horizon index, or named by any `cap` other than `cap N by <column>` alone. (Another table's sync audience can depend on the column only through a `read through` capture of the child's read rule, which the read-rule exclusion already covers.) |

Rationale for the `set null` exclusions: each one is a place where the
column's value is more than "which parent this row has". Clearing a column a
rule reads can grant or remove authority (`update <- .assignee = null`, or
another table's `exists grants[document = .id, folder = null]`), and the
parent's deleter was never authorized to change anybody's authority. An
immutable or field-owned column promises nobody else writes it. A recorded
or maintained path stores a fact resolved through the reference. A sync
audience or horizon would move the row between partitions. What remains is
the column that only says where a row is filed (a category, a folder used for
display, a "related to"). A reference the author's rules read chooses
`cascade`, `restrict` or `keep` instead. A self-reference may be `set null`;
it does not recurse.

**A cap on a `set null` column does not count null.** `cap N by category`
bounds each category's rows; rows whose `category` is null belong to no
parent and are not a group. This is new semantics only for a column that
declares `set null` (a cap on any other nullable column keeps counting its
null group as today), and it is what makes the cap a bound on the
reference's children rather than a limit that the set-null writes would
themselves overflow. Because the null group is then unbounded, **such a cap
never proves a population bound** (a loop's bound, a page's completeness,
mutation admission): those proofs ignore it, as they ignore an index that is
not unique. (A proof that the pinned value is non-null could recover the bound
for one parent's group; §10 records it.) Cap enforcement, activation's group validation, and a device's
cap proofs skip the null group of that column; changing the action away from
`set null` re-validates the cap at activation, null group included.

The unique inference has the same per-parent scope. It applies to required
and optional references: a plain unique reference has at most one row for each
non-null parent id. An optional unique reference may still have an unbounded
null group. Referential actions probe only a concrete non-null parent id, so
that null group is never counted in the action reservation and the inference
never proves a table population bound. When both declarations exist, the
effective bound is the smaller of the explicit cap and one.

### 2.3 The reference index

Every reference whose action probes or writes its children is probed by its
column. The binder reuses a plain index whose leading columns are the
reference (then, for an expiring child, its **effective** deadline column: a
`read through` child's captured `$deadline`, which is the earlier of its own
and its parents' deadlines, else its `expire at` column); otherwise it
synthesizes an engine-named one: `[column, id]`, or
`[column, deadlineColumn, id]` for an expiring child, so one seek skips
an expired backlog (as `read through`'s child index does, LLP 3000.014 §6):
the live rows are exactly `[id, null]` (never expires) and `[id]` with the
deadline after now, so both seeks start at the live suffix and no expired row
is ever visited.
A `read through` reference uses its existing child index. The same index
serves `cap N by <column>`. A `keep` reference gets none.

## 3. What a delete does

A delete of row `p` of table `P` — `delete P[id]`, `delete row`, a unique-key
`delete P[key = …]`, a job, `POST /seed`'s delete, or `snapback4 data` —
runs these steps in the deleting transaction, on every host:

1. **Find and authorize `p`**, as today, with one addition: when any
   `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference names `P`, the caller needs
   **read authority on `p`** as well as delete authority, for every delete
   attempt, with or without children. A caller who may delete but not read
   gets the ordinary hidden-target refusal. This is LLP 3000.014 §3.1's
   rule, generalized from `read through` children to every referenced table,
   and it keeps step 3 from probing a hidden row's children. The system
   principal passes both rules, as it does every rule.
2. **Reserve.** Charge the reservation `R(P)` of §5.1 on every meter, draw
   its row count from the request's physical authorization allowance, and
   publish the schema-fixed trace of §4.2.
3. **Close.** Starting from `p`, follow every `cascade` reference to the
   live rows that reference a reached row, and repeat: the **closure** `S`
   is `p` plus every row reached. (`S` is finite: the cascade graph is
   acyclic and each edge has an explicit or inferred effective bound.) Steps 3–5 stream the referencing rows

   the **first occupied reference in schema order** of
   `(child table, column)` — never the first found while walking hidden
   rows:

   `E_REFERENCED: projects at <site> is still referenced through comments.task (on delete restrict); delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)`

   "Live" means present and not expired. A row inserted earlier in the same
   transaction counts; one deleted earlier in it does not. Because rows in
   `S` are excluded, a diamond (`A` cascades to `B` and `C`, and `C`
   restricts `B`) or a self-referencing child table deletes when the whole
   closure goes together, as SQL's statement-end `NO ACTION` does. A `read
   through` reference is not part of this pass: it keeps its own refusal,
   `E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN`, and its stricter physical-child probe (LLP
   3000.014 §3.3), evaluated as each row of `S` is removed in step 6. When
   both would refuse, `E_REFERENCED` comes first (step 4 runs before any
   removal).
5. **Set null.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `set null` reference into
   `s`'s table, clear the column of each live referencing row **not in
   `S`** (deletion dominates: a row that is going away is not rewritten).
   Each reference's group is gathered whole (ids only, at most its effective
   bound: the explicit cap or inferred one)
   before any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling whose
   maintained column shares the reference's index and move it behind a page
   cursor. The write rereads the row's current image immediately before clearing it
   (an earlier clear's maintained write may have changed it), consults no
   rule, and applies its constraints, maintains and partition events as any
   write does.
6. **Delete.** Remove the rows of `S` other than `p`, each table before every
   table it must not outlive: its cascade parents and its `read through`
   parent. Only those edges order the removal (an ordinary `restrict` or
   `set null` reference between rows of `S` imposes none, since step 4
   already cleared them), `check` refuses a cycle in their union
   (`E_REFERENCE_ACTION`; e.g. `B` cascades from `P`, `C` cascades from `B`,
   and `B` reads through `C`), and ties keep discovery order. Each row is
   removed from its current image, consulting no rule and applying
   constraints, maintains and partition events as any delete does. Then
   remove `p` as today, **from its current image too**: the actions may have
   changed it (a maintained column on `p` mirrors its children's removal), and
   a store removes index entries from the image it is given. Authorization
   stays the decision of step 1.

Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a
`restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and
nothing commits.

An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
image yet.

**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.

For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
earlier cascade and set-null writes. An unreadable expired predecessor does not
veto actionable retirement. If the table declares a read-through child, a
writer who cannot read the predecessor receives the insert's ordinary rule
refusal before the engine probes physical child occupancy; that occupancy
cannot disclose a hidden expired identity as a unique constraint.

This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the

   436	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   437	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   448	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }
   460	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }

   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}

    91	    ("calendar-month", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.indexes.values().any(|i| i.components.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Calendar(key) if key.civil()))))

    93	    ("calendar-schedule", |s| s.schedules.iter().any(|schedule| schedule.months > 0)),

    97	    ("branch-merge-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_merge)),
    98	    ("branch-membership-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership)),
    99	    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#15 — v2 fences metered uncapped discovery and row-id point lanes from v1 devices.

   101	    ("branch-pages-v3", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v3)),
   102	    ("branch-pages-v4", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v4)),

   110	
   111	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   112	    match kind {
   113	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   114	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   115	        _ => false,
   116	    }
   117	}
   118	
   119	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   120	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   121	    match rule {
   122	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   123	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   124	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   125	        _ => false,
   126	    }
   127	}
   128	
   129	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   130	    match rule {
   131	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   132	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   133	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   134	        _ => false,
   135	    }
   136	}

   138	impl Schema {
   139	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   140	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   141	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   142	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   143	    }
   144	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   145	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   146	    }
   147	}
   148	
   149	impl Serialize for Schema {
   150	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   151	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   152	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   153	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   154	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   155	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   156	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   157	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   158	        }
   159	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   160	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   161	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   162	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   163	    }
   164	}
   165	
   166	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
   167	    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
   168	        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
   169	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
   170	        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   171	        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
   172	        let mut carriers = 0;
   173	        let mut legacy = false;
   174	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
   175	            let mut recorded = 0;
   176	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
   177	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
   178	                    carriers += 1;
   179	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
   180	                    false
   181	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   182	                    recorded += 1;
   183	                    false
   184	                } else { true }
   185	            });
   186	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
   187	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
   188	            }
   189	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   190	        }
   191	        for name in &declared {
   192	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
   193	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
   194	            }
   195	        }
   196	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
   197	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   198	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   199	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   200	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   201	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   202	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
   203	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
   204	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   205	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   206	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   207	            else { required.remove(cap); }
   208	        }
   209	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
   210	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
   211	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
   212	        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
   213	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
   214	            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
   215	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
   216	        }
   217	        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
   218	        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
   219	        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
   220	            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
   221	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
   222	        }
   223	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
   224	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
   225	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
   226	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
   227	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
   228	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
   229	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
   230	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
   231	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
   232	        }
   233	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
   234	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
   235	        }
   236	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
   237	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
   238	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
   239	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
   240	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
   241	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
   242	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
   243	        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
   244	        Ok(schema)
   245	    }
   246	}

     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on

    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is

    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is

    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.

    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))

     3	/-!

    10	namespace Quarry
    11	
    12	/-- An outcome. A query answers with data, `complete` and the returned
    13	page's continuation (`next`, null when none), or is unavailable (a cut
    14	scalar read), or refuses. A mutation commits a result and a new store, or
    15	refuses (and changes nothing). -/
    16	inductive Outcome where
    17	  | answer (data : Value) (complete : Bool) (next : Value)
    18	  | unavailable
    19	  | committed (result : Value) (store : Store)
    20	  | refused (code : String)

    22	/-- The world of a query: the view; every write refuses. -/
    23	def queryHooks : Hooks View where
    24	  view _ vw := vw
    25	  apply _ _ _ := throw (.refuse "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT")
    26	
    27	/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
    28	def storeHooks : Hooks Store where
    29	  view cx s := visibleRowsAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now
    30	  apply := applyWrite
    31	
    32	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
    33	/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
    34	is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
    35	sweep. -/

    37	
    38	structure MutationWorld where
    39	  store : Store
    40	  changed : ChangedRows := []
    41	
    42	/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.
    43	This retains a structurally identical expired replacement for commit-end
    44	retirement, while excluding `insert if absent` live-clash no-ops. -/
    45	def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
    46	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent => do
    47	    let td ← cx.schema.table? t
    48	    let fs ← (scalarsE fields).toOption
    49	    let rid ← (insertId fs).toOption

    51	    if ifAbsent && (findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now))

    53	    then none

    56	    match key.lookup "id" with
    57	    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    58	    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
    59	      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    60	      | _ => none
    61	  | _ => none

    63	def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
    64	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
    65	    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    67	    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)

    70	  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now

   111	
   112	structure Case where
   113	  schema : Schema
   114	  helpers : List Helper := []
   115	  store : Store
   116	  viewer : List Nat
   117	  now : Int := 0
   118	  program : Program

   122	  sweepOnly : Bool := false
   123	  /-- In-engine sweep continuation supplied by the differential driver. -/
   124	  sweepCursor : SweepCursor := {}
   125	  /-- Visited-row bound for the sweep; examples default to a complete pass. -/
   126	  sweepLimit : Option Nat := none
   127	
   128	def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
   129	  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
   130	    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }
   131	
   132	def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
   133	  | .normal => (.null, .null)
   134	  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)
   135	
   136	def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   137	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with

   139	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable

   141	    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now

   144	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   145	    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   146	
   147	def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   148	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   149	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   150	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   151	  | .ok env =>
   152	    match (execStmts mutationHooks defaultFuel c.ctx { store := c.store } env c.program.body).run {} with

   157	      | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   158	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   159	    | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"

   161	def run (c : Case) : Outcome :=

   163	    let (store, cursor) := sweepExpired c.schema c.store c.now c.sweepCursor c.sweepLimit

   166	    | .query => runQuery c
   167	    | .mutation => runMutation c
   168	
   169	end Quarry

9-//!
10-//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory

12-//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is

35-//! outcome; the canonical forms compared are its `continuation`.

5-//! `snapback4/lean/README.md`, "The case format").
6-//!
7-//! **Why the surface tree.** The model is a second implementation of the
8-//! binder and the interpreter together. Reading the binder's IR would copy
9-//! the binder's decisions into the model's input, and the comparison could
10-//! no longer find a binder defect. The input is the parsed [`Document`]s.
11-//! Besides the fact that [`crate::compile`] reported no diagnostics, the case
12://! carries the checked schema's selected plain expiry-index columns: that
13-//! physical choice determines observable cross-root action order and the
14-//! across-call continuation tuple. The emitter independently selects the first
15-//! eligible catalog entry; this qualifies execution given the planned index
16-//! catalog, not the planner's index synthesis. No program IR is read.
17-//!
18-//! **Types.** The few places that need a type (a text literal beside an id is
19-//! an id, OPEN V1; a positional key chooses a unique key by its argument

    49	fn validate_image(schema: &Schema, table_name: &str, row: &Value, viewer: Option<&str>, before_slots: bool, cache: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    50	    let table = schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
    51	    let object = row.as_object()?;
    52	    if !object.contains_key("id") {
    53	        return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name} row lacks id")));
    54	    }
    55	    if let Some(name) = object.keys().find(|name| !table.columns.contains_key(*name)) {
    56	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} row contains undeclared field {name}")));
    57	    }
    58	    for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
    59	        if before_slots && crate::schema::timeline::is_slot(name) { continue; }
    60	        if cache && matches!(name.as_str(), "value" | "recountPending") && !object.contains_key(name) { continue; }
    61	        let value = object.get(name).or_else(|| table.maintained.contains_key(name).then_some(&Value::Int(0)));
    62	        if value.is_none() && viewer.is_some_and(|viewer| table.written_by.get(name).is_some_and(|authority|
    63	            !authority.audience && row.field(&authority.owner).ok() != Some(&Value::Id(viewer.into())))) { continue; }
    64	        validate_column(table_name, name, kind, value)?;
    65	    }
    66	    for constraint in &table.constraints {
    67	        if let Constraint::Text { field, min, format } = constraint
    68	            && let Some(Value::String(text)) = object.get(field)
    69	        {
    70	            validate_text(&format!("{table_name}.{field}"), text, *min, *format).map_err(|error| RuntimeError::Constraint(error.to_string().trim_start_matches("E_INPUT: ").to_owned()))?;
    71	        }
    72	    }
    73	    Ok(())
    74	}

    98	fn validate_column_minimum(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>, label: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   117	fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {

   119	        Value::String(text) if text.chars().count() > 24 => format!("{} characters of text", text.chars().count()),
   120	        Value::String(text) => format!("the text '{text}'"),
   121	        Value::Id(id) => format!("the id '{id}'"),
   122	        Value::Int(n) => format!("the number {n}"),
   123	        Value::Bool(b) => format!("the boolean {b}"),
   124	        Value::Null => "null".into(),
   125	        Value::Bytes(b) => format!("{} bytes", b.len()),
   126	        Value::Array(items) => format!("a list of {}", items.len()),
   127	        Value::Row(_) | Value::Map(_) => "an object".into(),
   128	    }
   129	}

   162	pub(crate) fn fits(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> bool {
   163	    match (kind, value) {
   164	        (ColumnType::Optional(_), None | Some(Value::Null)) => true,
   165	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), Some(value)) => fits(inner, Some(value)),
   166	        (ColumnType::List { of, max } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, max, .. }, Some(Value::Array(values))) => values.len() <= *max as usize && values.iter().all(|value| fits(of, Some(value))),
   167	        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — typed references do not imply target existence
   168	        (ColumnType::Id | ColumnType::Principal | ColumnType::Ref { .. }, Some(Value::Id(_))) => true,
   169	        (ColumnType::Text { max }, Some(Value::String(text))) => text.chars().count() <= *max as usize,
   170	        (ColumnType::Bytes { max }, Some(Value::Bytes(bytes))) => bytes.len() <= *max as usize,
   171	        (ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. }, Some(Value::Map(fields))) => fields.get("id").is_some_and(|id| matches!(id, Value::Id(_))),
   172	        (ColumnType::Enum { variants }, Some(Value::String(value))) => variants.contains(value),
   173	        (ColumnType::Int | ColumnType::Time | ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value),
   174	        // @ref LLP 3000.040#14-where-the-bound-is-enforced — the slot's bound is part of its type: every stored write and argument meets it here.
   175	        (ColumnType::IntRange { min, max }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value) && (*min..=*max).contains(value),
   176	        (ColumnType::Bool, Some(Value::Bool(_))) => true,
   177	        (ColumnType::Json { max_bytes }, Some(value)) => canonical_json(value).len() <= *max_bytes as usize,
   178	        _ => false,
   179	    }
   180	}

   208	    Ok(())

   817	    /// Merge every authorized interval with one SQLite statement. The JSON
   818	    /// parameter is a relation of (partition, inclusive start, exclusive end, expiry),
   819	    /// so query count is independent of the number of held groups.
   820	    pub fn read_log_spans(&self, spans: &[(String, u64, Option<u64>, Option<i64>)], after: u64, only_seq: Option<u64>, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<LogEvent>, RuntimeError> {
   821	        let spans = serde_json::to_string(spans).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   822	        self.log_rows(
   823	            "SELECT l.seq, l.ord, l.t, l.kind, l.id, l.data FROM json_each(?1) AS span JOIN _log AS l
   824	             ON l.partition = json_extract(span.value, '$[0]')
   825	             AND l.seq >= json_extract(span.value, '$[1]')
   826	             AND (json_extract(span.value, '$[2]') IS NULL OR l.seq < json_extract(span.value, '$[2]'))
   827	             JOIN _commits c ON c.seq = l.seq
   828	             WHERE (json_extract(span.value, '$[3]') IS NULL OR c.at < json_extract(span.value, '$[3]')) AND l.seq > ?2 AND (?3 IS NULL OR l.seq = ?3) ORDER BY l.seq, l.ord LIMIT ?4",
   829	            &[&spans, &(after.min(i64::MAX as u64) as i64), &only_seq.map(|s| s.min(i64::MAX as u64) as i64), &(limit.min(i64::MAX as usize) as i64)])
   830	    }

   832	    fn log_rows(&self, sql: &str, params: &[&dyn rusqlite::ToSql]) -> Result<Vec<LogEvent>, RuntimeError> {
   833	        let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(sql)?;
   834	        let rows = statement.query_map(params, |row| {
   835	            Ok((row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as u64, row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as u32, row.get::<_, String>(2)?, row.get::<_, String>(3)?, row.get::<_, String>(4)?, row.get::<_, Option<String>>(5)?,
   836	            ))
   837	        })?;
   838	        rows.map(|row| {
   839	            let (seq, ord, table, kind, id, data) = row?;
   840	            let data = data.map(|data| serde_json::from_str(&data)).transpose().map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   841	            Ok(LogEvent { seq, ord, table, kind, id, data })
   842	        })
   843	        .collect()
   844	    }

    53	fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {
    54	    match (kind, value) {
    55	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => references(inner, value, out),
    56	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) => {
    57	            for value in values {
    58	                references(of, value, out);
    59	            }
    60	        }
    61	        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => out.push((table.clone(), id.clone())),
    62	        _ => {}
    63	    }
    64	}

    66	fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
    67	    kind: &ColumnType,
    68	    value: &mut Value,
    69	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    70	) -> bool {
    71	    match (kind, value) {
    72	        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
    73	            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
    74	            *id = next.clone();
    75	            true
    76	        }
    77	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
    78	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    79	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
    80	        _ => false,
    81	    }
    82	}

    85	    table: &Table,
    86	    row: &mut Value,

    88	) -> bool {
    89	    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return false };
    90	    table.columns.iter().fold(false, |changed, (column, kind)| {
    91	        fields.get_mut(column).is_some_and(|value| rewrite_legacy_reference(kind, value, ids)) || changed

   159	    tx: &Tx<'_>,

   161	    id: &str,

   163	    kind: &ColumnType,

   196	    )?;

   169	        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
   170	    ], 0).unwrap();
   171	    e.seed_delete("sequenced", "gone").unwrap();
   172	
   173	    let legacy7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
   174	    let legacy9 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(9)]);
   175	    let noncanonical7 = "[ { \"Int\" : 7 } ]".to_owned();
   176	    let wrong_type7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("7".into())]);
   177	    let schema = e.schema().clone();
   178	    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
   179	    let entries = schema.tables["entries"].clone();
   180	    let sequenced = schema.tables["sequenced"].clone();
   181	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   182	    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest7).unwrap().unwrap();
   183	    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
   184	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
   185	        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
   186	    }
   187	    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
   188	    tx.delete("totals", &target, &tx.get("totals", &digest9).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   189	    tx.delete("entries", &entries, &tx.get("entries", "e9").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   190	    let old = tx.get("sequenced", "kept").unwrap().unwrap();
   191	    let mut next = old.clone();
   192	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   193	        fields.insert("total".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
   194	    }
   195	    tx.put("sequenced", &sequenced, &next, Some(&old)).unwrap();
   196	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy7, 7).unwrap();
   197	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest7, 4).unwrap();
   198	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy9, crate::value::I53_MAX).unwrap();
   199	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest9, 12).unwrap();
   200	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &noncanonical7, 13).unwrap();
   201	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &wrong_type7, 14).unwrap();
   202	    tx.set_sequence("ordinary", &legacy7, 11).unwrap();
   203	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   204	    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
   205	
   206	    let next = compile(SOURCE);
   207	    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
   208	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   209	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy7).unwrap(), 0);
   210	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy9).unwrap(), 0);
   211	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest7).unwrap(), 7, "the deleted allocating row and lower destination counter cannot lower the high-water mark");
   212	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX);
   213	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &noncanonical7).unwrap(), 13, "a noncanonical dangling id must not collapse into the real group");
   214	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &wrong_type7).unwrap(), 14, "a canonical tuple with the wrong predecessor type stays opaque");
   215	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("ordinary", &legacy7).unwrap(), 11, "translation is scoped by parent table and id");
   216	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   217	    let kept = e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().pop().unwrap();
   218	    assert_eq!(kept.field("total").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest7.clone()));
   219	    assert_eq!(kept.field("ordinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(2));
   220	
   221	    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7))]))], 2).unwrap();
   222	    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().into_iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("next".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
   223	    let error = e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("full".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest9.clone()))]))], 2).unwrap_err();
   224	    assert_eq!(error.refusal().code, "E_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED");
   225	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   226	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX, "overflow refusal must not change the migrated counter");
   227	    tx.rollback().unwrap();
   228	}

   231	fn sequence_identity_adoption_keeps_invalid_canonical_groups_opaque() {
   232	    const SOURCE: &str = "table owners:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  label: text 3..20 format handle\n  owner: owners\n  public\nview labelTotals: count entries by .label\n  public\nview ownerTotals: count entries by .owner\n  public\ntable labelSequence:\n  parent: labelTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\ntable ownerSequence:\n  parent: ownerTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
   233	    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
   234	    let valid = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("valid_1".into())]);
   235	    let invalid_control = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("\u{1}".into())]);
   236	    let invalid_format = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("Not_A_Handle".into())]);
   237	    let invalid_reference = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id("x".repeat(136))]);
   238	    let valid_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("valid_1".into())]);
   239	    let control_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("\u{1}".into())]);
   240	    let format_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("Not_A_Handle".into())]);
   241	    let reference_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id("x".repeat(136))]);
   242	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   243	    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &valid, 5).unwrap();
   244	    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &invalid_control, 6).unwrap();
   245	    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &invalid_format, 7).unwrap();
   246	    tx.set_sequence("ownerTotals", &invalid_reference, 8).unwrap();
   247	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   248	    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
   249	
   250	    let next = compile(SOURCE);
   251	    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
   252	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   253	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("labelTotals", &valid).unwrap(), 0);
   254	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("labelTotals", &valid_digest).unwrap(), 5, "a fully admitted predecessor group migrates");
   255	    for (parent, old, digest, high) in [
   256	        ("labelTotals", &invalid_control, &control_digest, 6),
   257	        ("labelTotals", &invalid_format, &format_digest, 7),
   258	        ("ownerTotals", &invalid_reference, &reference_digest, 8),
   259	    ] {
   260	        assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value(parent, old).unwrap(), high, "invalid canonical tuple retains opaque custody");
   261	        assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value(parent, digest).unwrap(), 0, "invalid canonical tuple does not create digest custody");
   262	    }
   263	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   264	
   265	    e.seed_at([
   266	        ("labelSequence".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("control".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(invalid_control))])),
   267	        ("labelSequence".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("format".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(invalid_format))])),
   268	    ], 2).unwrap();
   269	    let label_rows = e.store().rows("labelSequence").unwrap();
   270	    assert_eq!(label_rows.iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("control".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(7)));
   271	    assert_eq!(label_rows.iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("format".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
   272	}

   391	fn surviving_aggregate_identity_wins_over_a_counter_only_dependency() {
   392	    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable cEntries:\n  parent: bTotals\n  public\nview cTotals: count cEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
   393	    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
   394	    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
   395	    e.seed_at([
   396	        ("aEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("a".into())), ("key", Value::Int(5))])),
   397	        ("bEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("b".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(digest_a.clone()))])),
   398	    ], 0).unwrap();
   399	    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
   400	    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a.clone())]);
   401	    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
   402	    let dangling_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
   403	    let legacy_c = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_b.clone())]);
   404	    let digest_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(dangling_b.clone())]);
   405	    let redirected_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_b.clone())]);
   406	    let schema = e.schema().clone();
   407	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   408	    tx.delete("aTotals", &schema.tables["aTotals"], &tx.get("aTotals", &digest_a).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   409	    tx.delete("aEntries", &schema.tables["aEntries"], &tx.get("aEntries", "a").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   410	    let old_source = tx.get("bEntries", "b").unwrap().unwrap();
   411	    let mut next_source = old_source.clone();
   412	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next_source {
   413	        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
   414	    }
   415	    tx.put("bEntries", &schema.tables["bEntries"], &next_source, Some(&old_source)).unwrap();
   416	    let mut target = tx.get("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap().unwrap();
   417	    tx.delete("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target).unwrap();
   418	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut target {
   419	        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy_b.clone()));
   420	        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
   421	    }
   422	    tx.put("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target, None).unwrap();
   423	    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 7).unwrap();
   424	    tx.set_sequence("cTotals", &legacy_c, 11).unwrap();
   425	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   426	    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
   427	
   428	    let next = compile(SOURCE);
   429	    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
   430	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   431	    assert!(tx.get("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap().is_some());
   432	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
   433	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap(), 7, "counter custody follows the surviving rebuilt parent");
   434	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 0, "the absent dependency cannot redirect custody");
   435	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &legacy_c).unwrap(), 0);
   436	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &digest_c).unwrap(), 11, "counter-only dependents inherit the authoritative surviving parent map");
   437	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &redirected_c).unwrap(), 0);
   438	    tx.rollback().unwrap();
   439	    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(dangling_b))]))], 2).unwrap();
   440	    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
   441	}

   546	    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
   547	    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so

   549	    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

   551	        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);

   567	    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Maintained aggregate identity
     5	
     6	The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
     7	tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
     8	cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
     9	store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
    10	lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
    11	and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
    12	identity while publishing the new version.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	namespace Quarry
    16	
    17	/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
    18	migration. -/
    19	def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
    20	
    21	/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
    22	not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
    23	to this logical model. -/
    24	def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
    25	  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
    26	    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
    27	    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
    28	
    29	theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
    30	  simp [maintainedIdV1]
    31	
    32	/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
    33	byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
    34	theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
    35	  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
    36	  omega
    37	
    38	def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
    39	  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
    40	
    41	structure MaintainedState where
    42	  version : Nat
    43	  rows : List Row
    44	
    45	/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
    46	identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
    47	states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
    48	def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
    49	    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
    50	  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
    51	
    52	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    53	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
    54	
    55	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    56	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
    57	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
    58	
    59	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    60	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
    61	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]

    63	/-! Persisted `sequence by` counters are server custody keyed by the parent
    64	table and physical parent id. They outlive allocating rows. This small model
    65	does not model SQL or the device protocol; it states the adoption invariant
    66	for one target-specific legacy-to-digest key. -/
    67	
    68	def sequenceHighWater (id : List Nat) (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
    69	  counters.foldl (fun high counter =>
    70	    if counter.1 = id then max high counter.2 else high) 0
    71	
    72	/-- If a partially upgraded store already has both keys, adoption merges them
    73	at their maximum. No child-row population participates in this value. -/
    74	def adoptedSequenceHighWater (legacy digest : List Nat)
    75	    (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
    76	  max (sequenceHighWater legacy counters) (sequenceHighWater digest counters)
    77	
    78	theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_legacy (legacy digest counters) :
    79	    sequenceHighWater legacy counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
    80	  Nat.le_max_left _ _
    81	
    82	theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_digest (legacy digest counters) :
    83	    sequenceHighWater digest counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
    84	  Nat.le_max_right _ _

    86	/-- A surviving aggregate row fixes the physical parent that rebuilt rows and

    94	    adoptedSequenceParent (some rowParent) counterOnlyParent = rowParent := by

    97	/-! SQL adoption supplies the predecessor column-admission verdict. This
