     1	/-!
     2	# Wave 12 device-queue contract witnesses
     3	
     4	This module is an independent, abstract contract witness for the device queue
     5	boundary. It is deliberately not part of `Quarry.Eval`, and it does not claim
     6	that the Lean row oracle models device prediction, sync, maintained-column
     7	projection, or the production meter.
     8	
     9	The first witness gives two server worlds with the same public rows and the
    10	same confirmed maintained total. Their withheld maintained predicates differ,
    11	so retiring the same parent produces different authoritative totals. No
    12	point-valued function of the public observation can be right in both worlds;
    13	queueing preserves the confirmed image until server catch-up.
    14	
    15	The second witness models only the law of the separate device physical-work
    16	allowance: nested work consumes the remainder from earlier work. Resetting the
    17	allowance between nested proofs would accept costs 2 and 3 under a limit of 4,
    18	while sequential consumption queues the second proof.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	namespace Quarry.Wave12DeviceQueue
    22	
    23	-- @ref LLP 3000.039#64-devices-and-prediction — private maintains and nested proof work queue when public device state cannot decide them within one allowance.
    24	
    25	inductive Kind where
    26	  | a
    27	  | b
    28	  deriving DecidableEq
    29	
    30	structure SourceRow where
    31	  id : Nat
    32	  parent : Nat
    33	  kind : Kind
    34	  deriving DecidableEq
    35	
    36	structure PublicRow where
    37	  id : Nat
    38	  parent : Nat
    39	  deriving DecidableEq
    40	
    41	structure PrivateWorld where
    42	  rows : List SourceRow
    43	  counted : Kind
    44	
    45	def publicProjection (rows : List SourceRow) : List PublicRow :=
    46	  rows.map fun row => ⟨row.id, row.parent⟩
    47	
    48	def total (world : PrivateWorld) : Nat :=
    49	  (world.rows.filter fun row => row.kind == world.counted).length
    50	
    51	def retireParent (parent : Nat) (world : PrivateWorld) : PrivateWorld :=
    52	  { world with rows := world.rows.filter fun row => row.parent != parent }
    53	
    54	def rows : List SourceRow := [
    55	  { id := 10, parent := 1, kind := .a },
    56	  { id := 20, parent := 2, kind := .b }
    57	]
    58	
    59	def countsA : PrivateWorld := ⟨rows, .a⟩
    60	def countsB : PrivateWorld := ⟨rows, .b⟩
    61	
    62	def confirmedTotal : Nat := 1
    63	
    64	def publicObservation (world : PrivateWorld) : List PublicRow × Nat :=
    65	  (publicProjection world.rows, confirmedTotal)
    66	
    67	example : publicObservation countsA = publicObservation countsB := rfl
    68	example : total countsA = confirmedTotal := rfl
    69	example : total countsB = confirmedTotal := rfl
    70	example : total (retireParent 1 countsA) = 0 := rfl
    71	example : total (retireParent 1 countsB) = 1 := rfl
    72	
    73	/-- A device point-predictor sees only public rows and the confirmed total. -/
    74	abbrev PointPredictor := List PublicRow → Nat → Nat
    75	
    76	/-- The indistinguishable worlds require different post-retirement totals, so
    77	one public point prediction cannot be authoritative in both. -/
    78	theorem projection_queues
    79	    (predict : PointPredictor) :
    80	    predict (publicProjection rows) confirmedTotal ≠ total (retireParent 1 countsA) ∨
    81	      predict (publicProjection rows) confirmedTotal ≠ total (retireParent 1 countsB) := by
    82	  have hA : total (retireParent 1 countsA) = 0 := rfl
    83	  have hB : total (retireParent 1 countsB) = 1 := rfl
    84	  rw [hA, hB]
    85	  omega
    86	
    87	inductive Decision where
    88	  | point (value : Nat)
    89	  | queue
    90	  deriving DecidableEq
    91	
    92	def soundFor (decision : Decision) (world : PrivateWorld) : Prop :=
    93	  match decision with
    94	  | .point value => value = total (retireParent 1 world)
    95	  | .queue => True
    96	
    97	theorem queue_is_sound_for_both_worlds :
    98	    soundFor .queue countsA ∧ soundFor .queue countsB := by
    99	  simp [soundFor]
   100	
   101	theorem no_point_is_sound_for_both_worlds (value : Nat) :
   102	    ¬ (soundFor (.point value) countsA ∧ soundFor (.point value) countsB) := by
   103	  simp [soundFor, countsA, countsB, rows, total, retireParent]
   104	  omega
   105	
   106	/-- Queueing publishes no speculative replacement for the confirmed image. -/
   107	def presentedTotal (confirmed : Nat) : Decision → Nat
   108	  | .point value => value
   109	  | .queue => confirmed
   110	
   111	example : presentedTotal confirmedTotal .queue = 1 := rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Spend `cost` from the remaining physical-work allowance. -/
   114	def spend (remaining cost : Nat) : Option Nat :=
   115	  if cost ≤ remaining then some (remaining - cost) else none
   116	
   117	theorem nested_spends_fit
   118	    {initial first second afterFirst afterSecond : Nat}
   119	    (hFirst : spend initial first = some afterFirst)
   120	    (hSecond : spend afterFirst second = some afterSecond) :
   121	    first + second ≤ initial := by
   122	  simp [spend] at hFirst hSecond
   123	  omega
   124	
   125	def nestedDecision (initial first second : Nat) : Decision :=
   126	  match spend initial first with
   127	  | none => .queue
   128	  | some remaining =>
   129	      match spend remaining second with
   130	      | none => .queue
   131	      | some _ => .point confirmedTotal
   132	
   133	/-- Resetting to the initial allowance between nested proofs would accept both
   134	individual costs even though their sum exceeds the request allowance. -/
   135	def resetWouldAccept (initial first second : Nat) : Bool :=
   136	  first ≤ initial && second ≤ initial
   137	
   138	example : resetWouldAccept 4 2 3 = true := rfl
   139	example : 4 < 2 + 3 := by decide
   140	example : nestedDecision 4 2 3 = .queue := rfl
   141	example : nestedDecision 5 2 3 = .point confirmedTotal := rfl
   142	
   143	end Quarry.Wave12DeviceQueue

    11	const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";

    13	/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
    14	/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
    15	/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
    16	pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    17	    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    18	    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
    19	) -> Vec<String> {
    20	    let after = cursors
    21	        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
    22	        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
    23	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    24	    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
    25	        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
    26	        tables.rotate_left(next);
    27	    }
    28	    tables
    29	}

    35	/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for

    37	pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    38	    schema: &Schema,
    39	    rows: I,
    40	) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
    41	where
    42	    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    43	    I::IntoIter: 'a,
    44	{
    45	    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {
    46	        return Box::new(rows.into_iter());
    47	    }
    48	    let order = schema.through_order();
    49	    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    50	    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));

    64	fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    65	    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {
    66	        let mut end = text.len().min(256);
    67	        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
    68	            end -= 1;
    69	        }
    70	        &text[..end]
    71	    }

    73	        let id = row
    74	            .field("id")
    75	            .ok()
    76	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    77	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");

    79	            .field(reference)
    80	            .ok()
    81	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
    82	            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
    83	        samples.push(format!(
    84	            "{}: {reference} -> {parent}[{}]",
    85	            bounded(id),
    86	            bounded(value)

    76	    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    77	        let name = namespace(name)?;

    79	        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    80	        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
    82	        }
    83	        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
    84	        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
    85	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    86	        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
    87	        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
    88	        if let Some(row) = client.query(

    90	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
    91	        )?.first() {

The counter migration uses predecessor aggregate definitions, preserves surviving-row mappings during counter settlement, and max-merges counters within each parent table. PostgreSQL performs the upgrade under its writer-head lock. I’m checking the remaining compatibility and coverage edges; I haven’t identified a material defect so far.

+#[test]
+fn legacy_semantic_backend_is_server_adoptable_but_device_refused() {
+    for (capability, source) in [
+        ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n"),
+        ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", "table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete cascade\n  cap 1 by parent\n  public\n"),
+    ] {
+        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+        let backend = Backend { generation: 1, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+        let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
+        for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+            for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+                if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                    names.retain(|value| value != capability);
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        let adopted: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy["schema"].clone()).unwrap();
+        assert!(adopted.legacy_semantic_capabilities.contains(capability));
+        assert!(serde_json::to_string(&adopted).unwrap().contains(capability));
+        let opening = Opening::parse(Some(&legacy.to_string())).expect("legacy bytes remain decodable for store migration");
+        let error = match opening.open(MemoryStore::new()) {
+            Err(error) => error,
+            Ok(_) => panic!("device executed backend missing {capability}"),
+        };
+        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+        assert!(error.to_string().contains(capability), "{error}");
+    }
+}
+
+fn legacy_digest_store<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) -> Backend {
+    let source = "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n";
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut current = Backend { generation: 2, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&current).unwrap();
+    legacy["generation"] = json!(1);
+    for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let old: Backend = serde_json::from_value(legacy.clone()).unwrap();
+    store.install(&old.schema, &BTreeMap::from([
+        ("device:backend".into(), legacy.to_string()),
+        ("device:generation".into(), "1".into()),
+    ]), false).unwrap();
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.outbox_insert(1, "pending", r#"{"id":"pending","seq":1,"op":"write","args":{},"new_ids":[]}"#).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    current.generation = 2;
+    current
+}
+
+fn legacy_digest_recovery<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S, initial: bool) {
+    let current = legacy_digest_store(store);
+    let error = match Opening::Kept.open(Borrowed(store)) {
+        Err(error) => error,
+        Ok(_) => panic!("offline device executed a kept pre-digest backend"),
+    };
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    let before = tx.outbox_entries().unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let opening = if initial { Opening::Initial(current) } else { Opening::Install(current) };
+    drop(opening.open(Borrowed(store)).expect("a current backend must recover a kept legacy backend"));
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.outbox_entries().unwrap(), before, "semantic upgrade preserves queued writes");
+    assert_eq!(tx.meta("device:generation").unwrap().as_deref(), Some("2"));
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+}

+    }
+}

+}

+The same boundary applies when an authored delete or commit-end expiry action
+writes a source of a maintained column. Even if the device holds the complete
+reference closure, it queues the whole mutation with no predicted rows; the
+public projection cannot derive the private total. Server settlement and the
+following stream or snapshot publish the child action and mirrored parent
+value together. Actions whose written sources feed no maintained column remain
+eligible for prediction under their ordinary coverage and meter proofs.

-- The Postgres evaluation store has no activation API: no adoption parity is claimed.
+- The Postgres evaluation store has no general activation API. Its open-time
+  maintained-identity upgrade is nevertheless an atomic generation barrier for

+  private target under the digest identity, then mirrors every live parent,
+  before publishing the identity marker and generation. Other activation
+  parity remains unclaimed.

index 0000000000..a897b02634
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/expiry_maintained_columns.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+//! Expiry actions whose child writes feed a private maintained column must
+//! settle on the server: the public device schema has the price but not the
+//! private derivation that computes the new total (LLP 3000.007.001 §3.7).
+mod common;
+use common::*;
+use serde_json::json;
+use snapback4_core::{Context, WriteState, value::{Value, object}};
+use snapback4_device::{device::{Device, StreamPage}, store::DeviceStore};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"
+table groups:
+  total: count children by .group
+  public
+  sync public
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  group: groups
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation expire(parent: parents, group: groups):
+  insert children { id: 'born', parent, group }
+  update parents[parent] { until: 0 }
+query group(id: groups):
+  return groups[id] { total }
+"#;
+
+fn acquire<S: DeviceStore>(engine: &mut snapback4_core::Engine, device: &mut Device<S>) {
+    let mut after = None;
+    let mut first = true;
+    loop {
+        let page = engine.snapshot_acquisition_page_at("alice", after.as_deref(), 100, 100).unwrap();
+        let next = page.next.map(|next| next.encode());
+        let page: StreamPage = serde_json::from_value(json!({
+            "snapshot":true, "after":after, "held":page.held, "acquisitions":page.acquisitions,
+            "events":page.events.iter().map(|event| json!({"table":event.table,"kind":event.kind.word(),"id":event.id,
+                "data":event.data.as_ref().map(snapback4_core::wire::to_json)})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+            "watermark":page.watermark, "more":next.is_some(), "next":next, "generation":engine.generation(),
+        })).unwrap();
+        device.apply(&page, first).unwrap();
+        let Some(next) = next else { break };
+        after = Some(next);
+        first = false;
+    }
+}
+
+fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(SOURCE);
+    server.seed_at([
+        ("groups".into(), object([("id", id("g"))])),
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("until", Value::Int(200))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut device = host.open("expiry-maintained-column", Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut server, &mut device);
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));
+
+    let error = device.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p","group":"g"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PREDICT", "{}: {error:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("children").len(), 1, "queued prediction publishes neither birth nor cascade");
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));
+
+    let from = server.seq().unwrap();
+    let outcome = server.mutate("expire", None, Context::new("alice", args(&[("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
+    device.apply(&stream_page(&mut server, "alice", from), false).unwrap();
+    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("children").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(0))]));
+    host.close("expiry-maintained-column", device);
+}
+
+#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_memory() { run(&mut Memory::new()); }
+#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_sqlite() { run(&mut Sqlite::new("expiry-maintained-column")); }

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}

   881	    fn final_exists_refusal(table_name: &str, constraint: &Constraint) -> RuntimeError {
   882	        let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, .. } = constraint else { unreachable!("final-exists witness names a final-exists constraint");
   883	        };
   884	        RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("inserting into {table_name} requires a matching row in {target} by the end of the mutation"))

   887	    /// `after insert <- exists t[...]` holds for every row inserted this
   888	    /// transaction; checked once the program has run.
   889	    pub(super) fn check_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   890	        let inserted = std::mem::take(&mut self.inserted);
   891	        for (table_name, row) in &inserted {
   892	            let constraints = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated").constraints.clone();
   893	            for constraint in &constraints {
   894	                if matches!(constraint, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. })
   895	                    && !self.final_exists_holds(table_name, row, constraint)? {
   896	                    return Err(Self::final_exists_refusal(table_name, constraint));
   897	                }
   898	            }
   899	        }
   900	        self.inserted = inserted;
   901	        Ok(())
   902	    }

   904	    /// Seed imports historically do not enforce every final-exists clause.
   905	    /// Capture only clauses that currently hold so seeded expiry retirement
   906	    /// can prove that its own reference actions did not invalidate them.
   907	    pub(super) fn satisfied_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<FinalExistsWitness>, RuntimeError> {
   908	        let inserted = self.inserted.clone();
   909	        let mut witnesses = Vec::new();
   910	        for (table, row) in inserted {
   911	            let constraints = self.schema.table(&table).expect("validated").constraints.clone();
   912	            for (constraint, clause) in constraints.iter().enumerate() {
   913	                if matches!(clause, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. })
   914	                    && self.final_exists_holds(&table, &row, clause)? {
   915	                    witnesses.push(FinalExistsWitness { table: table.clone(), row: row.clone(), constraint });
   916	                }
   917	            }
   918	        }
   919	        Ok(witnesses)
   920	    }
   921	
   922	    pub(super) fn check_final_exists_witnesses(&mut self, witnesses: &[FinalExistsWitness]) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   923	        for witness in witnesses {
   924	            let constraint = self.schema.table(&witness.table).expect("validated")
   925	                .constraints.get(witness.constraint).expect("captured constraint").clone();
   926	            if !self.final_exists_holds(&witness.table, &witness.row, &constraint)? {
   927	                return Err(Self::final_exists_refusal(&witness.table, &constraint));
   928	            }
   929	        }
   930	        Ok(())
   931	    }

   933	    fn contribution_heap(&self, table: &Table) -> u64 {
   934	        table.indexes.values().fold(0, |bytes: u64, index| match index.components.first() {
   935	            Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => bytes.saturating_add(
   936	                super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]).saturating_mul(16)),
   937	            _ => bytes,
   938	        })

   941	    fn charge_source_indexes(&mut self, table: &Table, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, mut entries: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   942	        for index in table.indexes.values() {
   943	            if let Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() {
   944	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps() * (u64::from(old.is_some()) + u64::from(new.is_some())))?;
   945	            }
   946	        }
   947	        if self.maintain_prepaid {
   948	            let id = old.or(new).expect("source image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   949	            for index in table.indexes.values() {
   950	                if matches!(index.components.first(), Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(_))) {
   951	                    let before = old.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   952	                    let after = new.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   953	                    let changed = before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)).count() + after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)).count();
   954	                    entries = entries.saturating_sub(changed as u64);
   955	                }
   956	            }
   957	        }
   958	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   959	        Ok(())
   960	    }

  1218	    pub fn snapshot_acquisition_page_at(&mut self, principal: &str, after: Option<&str>, limit: usize, now: i64) -> Result<partition::SnapshotPage, RuntimeError> {
  1219	        let now = self.advance_time_audience(now)?;
  1220	        let cursor = match after {
  1221	            Some(token) => Some(partition::SnapshotCursor::decode(token).ok_or_else(|| {
  1222	                RuntimeError::Input("the snapshot cursor is not one this server minted".into())
  1223	            })?),
  1224	            None => None,
  1225	        };
  1226	        let tx = self.store.read_transaction()?;
  1227	        let now = time_audience::observe_reader_time(&self.schema, &tx, now)?;
  1228	        let page = partition::snapshot_page(&tx, &self.schema, principal, cursor, limit, now)?;
  1229	        tx.rollback()?;

  1270	        seq: u64,
  1271	        limit: usize,

### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration

Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.

The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.

The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
`maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON of the group key —
atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate target from its source
rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
writer/head fence. Its narrowly admitted private maintained-column targets use
the same digest migration: rebuild the authoritative target and then mirror
every live parent before the marker or generation publishes. Before clearing
targets, adoption derives each target's
legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps, including
rows, columns and narrowed rows retained in release-dormant storage. Its
captured dormant-reference ledger changes in the same transaction, so a later
restore still proves the same aggregate lifetime under its digest address. Thus an
aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
Removing the aggregate itself retires its derived target rows; a dormant
reference to that retired target receives no map and keeps the ordinary
restore refusal against acquiring a newly created parent lifetime.

Persisted `sequence by` custody is part of the same identity migration even
when no allocating row, source row, or aggregate target row survives. Adoption
decodes canonical legacy counter ids with the predecessor aggregate's typed
group definition and admits every component through that predecessor source
column's complete value boundary: identity syntax and bounds, disallowed text
controls, required type and range/list bounds, plus declared text minimum and
format constraints. A canonical JSON tuple outside that domain remains an
opaque dangling parent id and keeps its original counter key. Admitted tuples
recursively settle any aggregate-reference components and re-key
`_sequences(parent, id, value)` through the resulting target-specific map. If legacy and digest keys both exist, their maximum high-water value wins;
the legacy key is removed and an exhausted counter remains exhausted. Counters
whose old parent also has a surviving aggregate row use that row-derived map;
independently decoded counter dependencies cannot redirect custody away from
the parent that rebuild and typed row-reference migration will address. This
preserves the ordinary dangling-reference contract when a grouped reference's
target is absent. Counters
for other parent tables and legacy strings that do not decode as a canonical
group tuple stay opaque. A predecessor aggregate removed by the candidate is
normalized before the current identity marker publishes, including when a
same-name row-keyed view temporarily replaces it; only a current ordinary
aggregate owns that counter identity domain. Later reintroduction therefore
cannot revive legacy custody under the marker. Counter rewrites
and their rollback share the adoption transaction with row-reference rewrites,
target rebuilds, marker and generation.

Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
the same transaction. A legacy target address is itself the predecessor's
canonical logical group tuple. Adoption decodes it using the predecessor
maintain and column types, so candidate projection cannot erase the migration
input when the same activation also changes the grouping declaration. The map
preserves the predecessor target identity; the candidate rebuild then decides
which new groups exist, so a reference to a removed group follows the ordinary
dangling-reference contract. The fixed-point bound counts stored aggregate identities,
not aggregate declarations, because one target can hold a legal acyclic chain
of references to other rows in that same target. SQLite captures newly recorded
path values while predecessor targets still exist, then derives and applies all
legacy maps before any recorded-path rebuild can remove those targets. Schemas
with ordinary maintains require device capability
`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
zero. Conversely, a current device refuses to execute backend bytes from an
old server that omit this capability. The shared codec records the omission so
writes and the root removal either commit together or roll back together. The same action
path governs a row born expired at commit and an expired predecessor retired
for a same-id insertion, so neither inline cleanup path can create an orphan.
When the table declares a read-through child, an unreadable predecessor
produces the insert's generic rule refusal before child occupancy is probed,
rather than disclosing its identity through a unique constraint; actionable
reference retirement alone does not require predecessor read authority.
Commit-end rows retire in reverse stable ancestor order (deeper read-through
tables, then lexically later peers, first) and ascending id order within a
table. This order is part of the transactional semantics: a restrict refusal
rolls back actions already applied to earlier rows rather than allowing
program statement order or map iteration order to choose the outcome.
Schema adoption clears both continuation layers. A successful development
reset clears them only after its empty-and-reseed transaction commits, so the
new store starts at the first table and key; a refused reset preserves the old
store's table and row continuation with all its other in-memory state.
Commit-end retirement and its actions precede `after insert` final-existence
checks. Those obligations therefore describe the actual provisional commit
state and cannot retain a witness that the same commit cascades away.

Expiring a never-opened root creates no root deletion event, because no device
could hold it. Its actions can still change opened children, and those ordinary
row changes carry their partition events. Deleting an opened row keeps the
ordinary revocation and retention semantics.
Expiry cleanup pins the authoritative floor but commits its physical removals
before attempting the next opening. A refused opening therefore cannot wedge
the cleanup that could make later progress possible.

## 7. Formal and generated semantics

The Lean table schema carries optional lower and upper lifetime fields. Its
`live` projection filters every logical row lookup, scan, probe and write result
at the case clock. Physical write-target lookup can still resolve an unopened,
unexpired row, but an expired target is `NOT_FOUND`; an ordinary insert or
upsert evaluates insert authority against the pre-retirement logical store,
retires an expired same-id predecessor with its referential actions, then checks
the new image's remaining unique keys against live occupants. `insert if absent`
preflights all of those live unique-key collisions before same-id retirement; a
collision is a no-op and preserves the expired predecessor and its children.
The emitter includes both lifetime fields and independently selects the first
eligible plain expiry index from the checked physical index catalog. This
qualifies sweep execution for the selected physical plan; it does not
independently re-prove the compiler's index synthesis. The model's explicit physical sweep
uses the same cascade/restrict/set-null closure as delete, retains a restricted
root and continues to later due rows. It eagerly rematerializes the declared
table snapshot after each retirement; this is extensionally the same sequential
store update while avoiding an exponential functional-update expression tree.
The formal sweep carries the same in-engine, across-call continuation as the server: the
last visited table rotates the next call even after a complete scan, and a
call stopped at its visited-row bound retains each table's last
`(selected index components,id)` key until the following call scans its tail
and wrapped head.
The Lean difftest generator preserves
seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.

The difftest AST and generator produce null/past/future/equal-boundary openings,
opening plus expiry, membership witnesses and caps. Its first formal fragment
has no prelude or separately seeded clock: rows are seeded and evaluated under
one operation clock with openings at null, clock-minus-one, clock, and
clock-plus-one. That fragment proves the pure `live(now)` projection without
claiming to model the durable pending ledger or its bounded publication loop.
Native runtime, simulator and both device-store lifecycle suites cover
lower/upper composition, publication, rescheduling, restart, hostile device
clocks and server-floor rollback.

## 8. Compiled recipe

The `time` and `recipes` cards carry one executable timed-disclosure recipe. It
states separately:

- use `not before .opensAt` to withhold a row until server time;
- use a mutation `require now <|>= deadline else CODE` to authorize a timed
  write;
- a nullable opening means immediately readable, and `expire at` is the
  independent upper boundary;
